title: Compiler/Runtime Upgrades Constrained by Paid Customer Versions
pattern: Delaying compiler or standard library upgrades across an entire codebase to support a small set of clients running on outdated runtimes.
why_bad: It holds the entire transitive closure of dependencies hostage, blocking security patches, optimizations, and modern language features across the ecosystem.
detection: Platform/compiler-specific configurations (`cfg` flags) retained exclusively to maintain compatibility with obsolete client environments.
counterexample: Deploying containerized virtualization environments to isolate legacy applications from core development.
fix: Separate the legacy application into an isolated runtime or enforce a sunset timeline for obsolete versions.
source: *Software Engineering at Google (Winters et al.), Chapter 21, p. 454 [194, 1045]*
